title: Region standby activation rehearsal & restore sanity tests
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Create and validate an end-to-end active->passive regional failover rehearsal that exercises: (1) standby region activation (networking, routing, DNS), (2) stateful backup restore for tokenstore and metadata, (3) circuit breaker and load-shedding behaviors under target load, and (4) SLO verification and post-dr metrics. The goal is a safe, repeatable playbook that the SRE and Platform teams can run quarterly with clear success criteria and rollback gates.
background: We operate a multi-region active-passive deployment for critical inference services. Previous drills exposed gaps in: restore verification time, KV cache warming, client-side retry semantics, and unclear ownership for circuit breaker parameters. This ticket formalizes a rehearsed path to bring standby online, validate backups, and confirm SLOs are met or that automatic fallback triggers correctly. Existing artifacts: tokenstore DR playbook (ENG-24001) and live swap procedures (ENG-23110); this work stitches those into a single rehearsal blueprint and adds measurable validation steps.
runbook_steps: Pre-drill checklist (48h): notify customers/internal stakeholders, schedule oncall rotation, snapshot current config, lower DNS TTL to 60s for test zone, confirm backup retention and recent successful backup manifest in S3.

Stage environment: provision isolated test CNAME and route 10% synthetic traffic via traffic switcher to standby. Ensure standby has identical runtime-1.24 binaries and model artifacts available (use artifact mirror).
Backup validation: verify latest backup manifest, run checksum compare for tokenstore and metadata bundles, validate KMS decrypt with staging key, and copy a point-in-time backup to a restore bucket.

Restore to staging cluster: bring up fresh instances in standby region using restore bucket, run database ingestion, run tokenstore integrity checks (consistency of keys, item counts, and a 1% random-entry content verification).
Promote standby read/write role: run leader promotion script under supervision; ensure writes are directed to promoted writer and that replication lag is below 2s before enabling clients.

Traffic ramp: start with 1% synthetic traffic, monitor error budgets, P99 latency, and circuit-breaker signals for 10m intervals. Increment to 25% if stable for 20m, then 100% for final validation window (max 1h).

Circuit breaker stress tests: inject service errors (5xx at 3% baseline and a 10% spike) and latency tail (increase downstream DB latency by 100ms) to validate automatic tripping and fallback behaviors. Observe that client SDKs receive 429s with retry-after where appropriate and fallback model variant routes are used.

Load-shedding validation: artificially exceed token generation QPS to trigger shedding thresholds; confirm responses degrade to summary-mode payloads for low-tier API keys and that high-tier keys are protected per policy.

Rollback gate: if error budget usage exceeds 20% of the drill window or P99 latency > 2x SLO, initiate automatic rollback: revert DNS, demote standby writer, and restore routing to primary. Log rollback reason and collect traces.

Post-drill: capture dashboards, export flamegraphs and traces to the incident bucket, run the restoration verification checklist, and schedule a retrospective within 5 business days. Create follow-up tickets for any action items.
Communication: send a consolidated summary to #sre-runbooks and product stakeholders within 24 hours with incident links and customer impact assessment.
acceptance_criteria: Standby region can accept read/write traffic for a sustained 30-minute window with SLOs within thresholds: availability >= 99.95% and P99 latency <= 300ms for inference endpoints under synthetic load.
Backup restore completes to staging and passes integrity checks (checksums and 1% content sample) within defined RTO of 60 minutes and RPO <= 1 hour.
Circuit breakers and load-shedding trigger at configured thresholds and client SDKs observe expected error semantics (429 with retry-after or structured fallback).
Rollback procedure validated: can revert to primary routing within 15 minutes without data loss and with clear post-rollback verification steps.
Playbook executed by a small cross-functional team (SRE, Platform, Oncall, PM) using only documented steps; all deviations are captured as action items.
Automated dashboards capture key metrics for the drill (error budget burn, RTO/RPO timings, replication lag, cache hit ratios) and persist the drill run for audit purposes.
monitoring_and_alerts: SLO dashboards: availability, P50/P95/P99 latency, error rate by service and region.
Circuit-breaker metrics: CB_state (closed/open/half-open), tripped_count, tripped_rate over 1m/5m windows.
Synthetic traffic probes for validation endpoints in standby region (heartbeat every 30s).
Pager thresholds for drill leads only: error_rate > 2% sustained for 5m, P99 latency > 500ms for 5m, replication_lag > 15s.
communication_plan: Pre-drill: announcement in #platform-ops, direct message to customer success for any customers with active incidents, update Status Page to 'Scheduled maintenance' limited to test zone.
During drill: live notes in runbook document, Slack thread for oncall, and a pinned Loom recording for significant manual steps.
Post-drill: summary message with pass/fail, metrics, and action items; send to execs and affected product teams; update runbook with any changes.
restore_validation_tests: Checksum parity: compare source backup SHA256 to restored objects for tokenstore and metadata bundles.
Functional verification: run 200 synthetic end-to-end requests that exercise token creation, KV reads, and embeddings lookup; assert response correctness and latency bounds.
Schema migration sanity: if restore lands on runtime-1.24, run DB migration dry-run and verify 0 migration conflicts.
Secrets/KMS sanity: decrypt 10 random secrets using staging KMS keys and ensure no missing key errors.
Smoke users: use non-prod test keys across different identity tiers to validate RBAC boundaries after promotion.
circuit_breaker_and_shedding_policies: Error-rate CB: trip if 5xx error rate > 2.0% over a 5-minute sliding window; auto-half-open after 60s.
Latency CB: trip if P99 latency > 1200ms for 3 consecutive 1-minute buckets.
Queue-depth CB: trip when request queue > 8000 pending tokens for more than 30s.

Load-shedding tiers: lowest-tier API keys are shed first (summary-mode responses), medium-tier receive prioritized batching, high-tier receive protected capacity and are routed to dedicated pools where configured.
Circuit-breaker telemetry must surface decision context (reason, triggering metric values, impacted routes) in traces.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: accidental promotion of standby in production namespace. Mitigation: use isolated test DNS entries and a manual approval gate for global promotion.
Risk: long restore times causing extended downtime. Mitigation: pre-copy recent backups to region and validate incremental restore speed; set RTO gates and abort criteria.
Risk: cache cold-start causing apparent latency spike. Mitigation: warm top-1000 keys via pre-warm script and measure cache hit ratio during ramp.
Risk: secrets not accessible in standby. Mitigation: verify KMS replication and test decryption prior to promotion.
post_dr_actions: Create follow-up tickets for any deviations observed with priority tags and owners assigned within 48h.
Update runbook steps and add automation for manual steps that exceeded estimated time by >25%.
Run a blameless retrospective and publish notes in Confluence within 5 business days.
Ingest recorded traces and logs into the retention archive for compliance audits.
